implementationPlan.description:
GREEN — THE NODE AUTHENTICATOR, as a new PowerShell script `tools/packaging/authenticate-node.ps1`. TWO design constraints decide this shape and neither is negotiable.
FIRST, THE VERIFIER MUST NOT BE NODE. Authenticating node by running a node program is circular: a substituted node can report any `--version` and any hash you ask it to compute about itself. The verifier therefore runs under pwsh, which the runner image provides, and resolves + hashes the node executable BEFORE any node process starts. State this in the file's docstring so nobody later 'simplifies' it into an .mjs.
SECOND, THE WORKFLOW HAS ~9 LINES OF HEADROOM (391 of a hard 400). Inlining version+digest verification into two steps costs 20-30 lines and breaks the cap. Extraction costs +1 line total: the ZIP step gains a `shell: pwsh` line and swaps its `run:`, and the evidence step swaps one line in place. The house precedent is the existing `run: tools/packaging/smoke-windows-artifact.ps1 -Zip dist/moe-windows.zip` step. Extraction also makes step 2's harness honest, because the harness can invoke the REAL script rather than a copy of the workflow's logic.
BEHAVIOUR: resolve node from the setup-node install (not a bare PATH lookup that a forged shim could win); read tools/packaging/toolchain-pins.json — the ONE source of truth, no literal version or digest in the workflow or in this script; compare `node --version` to nodeVersion as an EXACT ordinal string match (the pin carries the leading `v`); compare `Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256` of the resolved executable to nodeSha256, case-insensitively; refuse before spawning anything if either differs. Then invoke the entry with SHELL-FREE ARGV — an argument array through the call operator, never a composed command string. Pass PNPM_HOME through so half A's packer handoff resolves without npm_execpath. Refuse with the exact code and `@WINDOWS_RELEASE_AUTHORITY` layer chosen in step 4. Verify Get-FileHash and node:crypto agree on the same bytes for the same file, since the harness will cross-check.
implementationPlan.note: tools/packaging/authenticate-node.ps1 (130 lines, pwsh not node - non-circular by construction, stated in docstring). Reads tools/packaging/toolchain-pins.json only; zero literal version/digest. Resolves node from RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE/node/<ver>/<arch>/node.exe (not PATH), rejects reparse points/containers/path escapes. Get-FileHash SHA256 vs pins.nodeSha256 (ordinal-ignore-case) BEFORE any node spawn; then ordinal-exact `node --version` vs pins.nodeVersion. Shell-free argv via call operator with a [string[]] array. Removed a debug Get-PSCallStack print that leaked internal function names into the refusal output. Drills (all exit 1, code@layer exact): tool cache unset -> WINDOWS_RELEASE_INPUT_INVALID@WINDOWS_RELEASE_AUTHORITY; correct version + wrong nodeSha256 -> WINDOWS_RELEASE_NODE_DIGEST_MISMATCH@WINDOWS_RELEASE_AUTHORITY; correct digest + wrong nodeVersion -> WINDOWS_RELEASE_VERSION_MISMATCH@WINDOWS_RELEASE_AUTHORITY. Those last two are DISJOINT divergence inputs, so digest and version are separately load-bearing rather than one fence answering for both. Get-FileHash and node:crypto agree byte-for-byte on the resolved executable and both equal the pin (b3094d0b...0aa3). Harness `node --test tests/integration/release/release-supply-chain.test.mjs` = EXIT 0, `tests 1 / pass 1 / fail 0`. NOTE for step 4: the :708 vocabulary arm scans candidateSource (workflow YAML only), so the authenticator's codes are currently UNSCANNED - step 4 must both add WINDOWS_RELEASE_NODE_DIGEST_MISMATCH to the frozen allow-set and extend the scanned surface to the authenticator.

DRILL R3-12-E (contract): restore the ZIP step to `run: pnpm pack:windows` -> the named step-2 arm reds; separately delete ONLY the SHA256 comparison from the authenticator -> the digest arm reds and the version arm stays green. Two drills, disjoint arm sets: that disjointness is what proves the version check and the digest check are separately load-bearing rather than one fence answering for both.
DRILL R3-12-F (end-to-end): in a %TEMP% COPY of the tree — never the shared worktree — revert half A's runner digest check, run the identical harness, and require it to PRODUCE the forged ZIP (arm red, `FORGED_PNPM_EXECUTED` observed). This is the drill that proves the harness can actually observe the forgery; without it, an assertion that the ZIP is absent passes identically against a harness whose forged pnpm was never reachable in the first place.
CONTROL, and do not skip it: confirm the forged pnpm was genuinely FIRST on PATH and at PNPM_HOME during the passing run — print the resolved pnpm path from inside the harness. A harness that silently failed to stage its forgery asserts nothing.
A GREEN drill is a FINDING to report in a comment and stop on, never a pass to bank.
